Biallelic pathogenic variants in TRAPPC12 (also known as TTC15) reduce the amount or activity of the TRAPPC12 protein, a subunit of the TRAPP (transport protein particle) membrane-tethering complex. Reported alleles include frameshift/null variants (c.145delG [p.Glu49Argfs], c.360dupC [p.Glu121Argfs]) and missense variants (c.1880C>T [p.Ala627Val], c.679T>G [p.Phe227Val]). Because complete loss is expected to be embryonic lethal, surviving individuals carry at least one hypomorphic allele; the most severe (compound-heterozygous) genotypes have been reported in fetuses with hydrocephaly and recurrent pregnancy loss. Beyond its membrane-trafficking role, TRAPPC12 (the alias TRAMM denotes "trafficking of membranes and mitosis") also participates in mitosis/kinetochore function and in ciliogenesis, but the human encephalopathy phenotype is most directly linked to the secretory-trafficking defect.

nodes.description: The TRAPP complex is a multisubunit membrane-tethering complex conserved from yeast to humans that functions as a guanine-nucleotide-exchange factor (GEF) for Rab GTPases: metazoan TRAPPIII (which contains TRAPPC12) activates Rab1, the master regulator of the early secretory pathway and autophagy, while TRAPPII activates Rab11 at the late Golgi. Reduced TRAPPC12 impairs this shared machine, lowering Rab-dependent tethering and activation at ER-to-Golgi and intra-Golgi steps.
